qmroot_binding.note: 6D absent; negative rungs absent; INV-013 = 0D only

description: Defines the five Book 7 (SARG) operators, their roles, invariant bindings, phase assignments, drift costs, sequence, and downstream handoffs to Books 8 and 9.

operators.name: NodeConstruct
operators.role: Constructs the formal argument structure A = ⟨N_A, R_A, C_A, root(A)⟩. Declares all nodes (Claims, Evidence, Warrants, Qualifiers, Rebuttals), assigns node types and provenance records, declares all structural relations in R_A, and performs the initial reachability partition (reach(A) and orphan_set). Loads upstream feeds from Book 6 GRL regime_status_report as structured Evidence nodes where applicable.
operators.input: Raw argument material: root claim declaration, evidence sources, provisional relation declarations; Book 6 regime_status_report (if governance-domain argument); Book 3 SD-Σd detection outputs (if argument pattern detection was invoked)
operators.output: Formal argument structure A with: N_A (typed nodes), R_A (declared relations), C_A (constraint set), root(A), reach(A), orphan_set
preconditions: init phase complete; all four dependency modules loaded
Root claim declared before SARG-Ν executes
TEL evaluation (TEL-Σ PASS) confirmed for all incoming structured expressions
postconditions: A is fully declared with all four tuple components
reach(A) and orphan_set are recorded in session state
All Evidence node provenance records are established
Book 6 GRL regime_status_report evidence has been loaded into N_A if applicable
A's TEL encoding is ready for submission to TEL-Σ
must_not: Proceed without a declared root(A) — root claim is mandatory before construction
Include orphan nodes in the reachable set
Accept an Evidence node as supporting a claim without declaring a Warrant relation (pre-empting INV-SARG-002)
Treat GRL regime_status_report narrative text as direct claim content — it must be converted to typed Evidence nodes
Skip provenance recording for any Evidence node

grl_feed_integration.description: When the argument concerns governance, legitimacy, or authority, SARG-Ν queries the Book 6 GRL-Σ regime_status_report and converts its fields into typed Evidence nodes with explicit provenance attribution.
grl_feed_integration.evidence_node_type: E[grl_evidence_ID]: derived from GRL-Σ output; provenance = book6_grl.regime_status_report

operators.notes: First active operator in every SARG evaluation session. No other SARG operator may execute before SARG-Ν completes. A construction failure (root not declared, R_A malformed) halts the session — no partial argument structures proceed to evaluation.

operators.name: WarrantAudit
operators.role: Audits the Warrant coverage of the constructed argument A. For every claim-evidence pair in reach(A), verifies that at least one declared Warrant node bridges the evidence to the claim. Produces a complete warrant coverage report and flags all uncovered pairs as INV-SARG-002 violations.
operators.input: Argument structure A from SARG-Ν (reach(A), N_A, R_A); warrants set from N_A
operators.output: warrant_coverage_report: {covered_pairs: [...], uncovered_pairs: [...], coverage_rate: float ∈ [0,1]}; INV-SARG-002 violation list
preconditions: SARG-Ν has completed and A is fully declared
reach(A) is recorded and orphan_set is excluded
All Warrant nodes in N_A have declared source (Evidence) and target (Claim) fields
postconditions: warrant_coverage_report is recorded in session state
All uncovered CE pairs are recorded as INV-SARG-002 violations
If uncovered_pairs ≠ ∅: session records argument as invalid at EG-002 pending warrant addition
If uncovered_pairs = ∅: EG-002 passed; SARG-Δ may proceed
must_not: Accept an implicit warrant — every warrant must be a declared Warrant node in N_A
Infer warrant coverage from semantic proximity of claim and evidence content
Mark a CE pair as covered without verifying the Warrant node's source and target fields
Proceed to SARG-Δ if uncovered_pairs ≠ ∅ without recording the EG-002 failure
Treat positional adjacency of nodes in the argument graph as warrant coverage

tel_binding.description: SARG-Ω submits each Warrant node to TEL-Α for invariant assertion. TEL-Α confirms that the warrant bridge expression satisfies INV-TEL-001 (expressibility) and INV-TEL-002 (unambiguous denotation).
tel_binding.assertion: INV[SARG-002]: assert (∀(c,e) ∈ CE_pairs(A): ∃w ∈ W(A): (e ⊢ c) ∈ R_A)

operators.notes: Warrant coverage is the most common failure point in SARG evaluation. Many argument constructions supply evidence with implicit justification assumed from domain context. SARG-Ω enforces explicit declaration without exception. The coverage_rate field provides a diagnostic metric — a coverage_rate of 1.0 is required for EG-002 pass.

operators.name: DefeatCheck
operators.role: Processes all defeat attempts registered against argument A. Verifies that each defeat has a structural target in (nodes(A) ∪ R_A ∪ C_A), applies the defeat operation to the argument, recomputes reach(A) post-defeat, and reclassifies incomplete defeats as parallel assertions. Enforces INV-SARG-003 defeat completeness throughout.
operators.input: Argument A (post EG-002); session defeat log containing all registered defeat attempts D_1 ... D_k
operators.output: defeat_tally: {complete_defeats: [...], reclassified_as_parallel_assertions: [...], argument_post_defeat: A' (modified A), reach_post_defeat: reach(A')}; outcome per defeat ∈ {complete, reclassified, session_fault}
preconditions: EG-001 and EG-002 results are recorded
Session defeat log is accessible — may be empty (no defeats registered)
postconditions: Every registered defeat is classified as complete, reclassified, or session_fault
No defeat records remain in ambiguous state
reach(A') is recorded post-defeat
If all paths to root(A) are severed: eval_SARG = invalid; session records total collapse
Parallel assertion records (PA entries) are finalized and do not affect A validity
must_not: Allow a surface objection to modify A's validity status without structural target identification
Count a reclassified parallel assertion as a structural defeat
Apply a defeat operation without verifying that T_D ∈ (reach(A) ∪ R_A ∪ C_A) first
Skip recomputation of reach(A') after any defeat operation
Record a defeat against a node or relation not present in A (ghost defeat — DFM-003)

defeat_type_handling.DT-001_NodeDefeat: Suspend node; recompute reach; check for new orphans
defeat_type_handling.DT-002_WarrantDefeat: Suspend Warrant; re-run EG-002 on affected CE pair; record INV-SARG-002 status
defeat_type_handling.DT-003_RelationDefeat: Remove relation from R_A; recompute reach; check for new orphans
defeat_type_handling.DT-004_ConstraintDefeat: Evaluate meta-argument A_meta; if valid, suspend constraint from C_A; re-evaluate
defeat_type_handling.DT-005_UndercuttingDefeat: Apply scope restriction to Warrant; sever E→C path in this argument context

operators.notes: SARG-Δ is the most complex operator in the SARG cycle because defeat is a recursive operation — a Constraint Defeat (DT-004) requires running a full SARG evaluation on the meta-argument. Sessions must track evaluation depth to prevent infinite recursion. Maximum recommended defeat recursion depth: 3.

operators.name: ReachabilityAudit
operators.role: Performs the definitive reachability and reflexive prohibition audit on the post-defeat argument A'. Enumerates all cycles in reach(A'). For each cycle through root(A'), verifies the presence of at least one independent evidentiary node. Flags all prohibited reflexive loops. Produces the final reachability certification.
operators.input: Post-defeat argument A' from SARG-Δ; reach(A') computed by SARG-Δ; provenance records for all Evidence nodes in reach(A')
operators.output: reachability_certification: {reach_final: [...], cycles_detected: [...], prohibited_loops: [...], independent_evidence_verified: bool}; INV-SARG-004 violation list
preconditions: SARG-Δ has completed; defeat_tally is finalized
reach(A') is the definitive post-defeat reachable set
All Evidence node provenance records are available from SARG-Ν
postconditions: All cycles in reach(A') are enumerated and recorded
Each cycle through root(A') is assessed for independent evidence
prohibited_loops list is finalized (may be empty)
If prohibited_loops ≠ ∅: INV-SARG-004 violations recorded; argument is invalid
If prohibited_loops = ∅: EG-004 passed; proceed to EG-005 via SARG-Σ
must_not: Skip cycle enumeration on the assumption that argument graphs are acyclic — all graphs must be checked
Accept a derivation of root(A) as independent evidence of root(A)
Treat a restatement or elaboration of root(A)'s content as an independent evidentiary node
Proceed to SARG-Σ if any prohibited_loop remains unresolved
Conflate structural provenance independence with propositional independence

independence_verification.method: For each candidate independent Evidence node n_i on a cycle: check provenance(n_i) against derivation_closure(root(A)). Independence holds iff the intersection is empty.
independence_verification.derivation_closure_construction: derivation_closure(root(A)) is built by forward-tracing all nodes that were generated from, entailed by, or are logically subordinate to root(A)'s structural content. This is declared during SARG-Ν argument construction.

operators.notes: SARG-Ρ is the reflexivity guardian. Self-supporting arguments are the structural equivalent of self-governing regimes (INV-GRL-003) — they are paradox conditions that must be structurally resolved, not merely noted. A failed EG-004 always requires argument restructuring, not parameter adjustment.

operators.name: SynthesisOutput
operators.role: Final synthesis operator. Evaluates A' against all declared constraints in C_A (post-defeat, post-orphan-exclusion, post-prohibition-check). Produces the definitive evaluation result eval_SARG ∈ {valid, invalid, suspended}. Generates the argument_validity_report for downstream consumption by Books 8 and 9.
operators.input: Post-defeat A' from SARG-Δ; reachability_certification from SARG-Ρ; C_A constraint set; all gate results (EG-001 through EG-004)
operators.output: eval_SARG ∈ {valid, invalid, suspended}; argument_validity_report (complete structured output for downstream books); structural_argument_trajectory (for Book 9 PD); argument_templates (for Book 8 NoS)
preconditions: SARG-Ν, SARG-Ω, SARG-Δ, and SARG-Ρ have all completed
EG-001 through EG-004 results are all recorded
No gate result is in ambiguous or unresolved state
C_A constraint set is finalized (post-defeat constraint suspensions applied)
postconditions: eval_SARG is definitively recorded as valid, invalid, or suspended
argument_validity_report is available for downstream books
All constraint violations are documented in the report
All defeat records (complete and reclassified) are included in the report
structural_argument_trajectory is computed and packaged for Book 9 PD
must_not: Declare eval_SARG = valid if any gate result is failure or pending
Suppress constraint violation records in the argument_validity_report
Conflate SARG structural validity with propositional truth in the report
Forward a suspended argument to Book 8 or Book 9 without marking it as suspended
Include parallel assertion records as defeat records in the downstream report

book8_nos.description: Structurally valid argument templates produced by SARG-Σ provide Book 8 NoS with formal patterns for philosophical inquiry. The constraint satisfaction profiles of valid arguments inform meta-structural analysis of what makes structural arguments sound.

book9_pattern_dynamics.description: SARG-Σ computes the structural trajectory of A across evaluation cycles — how the argument evolved through construction, defeat, and re-evaluation. This trajectory is a pattern dynamics input for Book 9 PD, feeding attractor and bifurcation analysis of recurring argument structures.

gate_dependencies.SARG-Δ: requires SARG-Ω pass (EG-002) or explicit invalid record
gate_dependencies.SARG-Ρ: requires SARG-Δ complete and defeat_tally finalized
gate_dependencies.SARG-Σ: requires SARG-Ρ complete and all EG results recorded

operator_interaction_summary.parallelism: No SARG operators run in parallel — each depends on the prior operator's output. Within phases, supporting TEL operations (TEL-Σ, TEL-Ε, TEL-Α) may run in parallel with operator pre-checks.
